name: METR/eval-analysis-public
why: Code and run data behind the F1 time-horizon curves (logistic fit of success against log human minutes, hierarchical bootstrap, DVC pipelines per report version). Borrow: the method for turning our benchmark's per-task human-time estimates and pass/fail into a horizon number with a confidence interval; process lesson: METR versions each report (time-horizon-1-0, 1-1) so a changed method never silently overwrites old numbers. No license file, so read, do not copy.

name: McGill-DMaS/ODCV-Bench
why: 40 sandboxed bash scenarios where a KPI conflicts with a safety rule (F11), each in Mandated and Incentivized wording, scored by a four-model judge panel with the model's own runs judged by the other three. Borrow: the paired-prompt design and median-of-judges-excluding-self grading for our evaluator; lesson: its README reports Krippendorff alpha 0.81 for the panel and states the scenarios are synthetic, not deployment rates.

name: ccusage/ccusage
why: Reads Claude Code's local JSONL logs to report tokens and dollars (it has daily and monthly reports). Borrow: the per-run $ and token accounting for the kit's scorecard (F15 says /usage figures are list-price estimates); note it moved from ryoppippi/ccusage, and F12 warns cost columns can double-count nested calls, so cross-check its totals against the API invoice before trusting them.

name: TransluceAI/docent
why: Platform for reading agent transcripts at scale with custom rubrics; the tool HAL (F7) used to find shortcuts, tool-call failures and recovery rates in 2.5B tokens of logs. Borrow: rubric-over-transcripts as the auditor's method for finding why runs failed; license field reads NOASSERTION, so check LICENSE before copying.

name: langfuse/langfuse
why: Open-source tracing and cost tracking for LLM apps (traces, per-model cost, evals). Borrow: one trace per kit run with cost attached, as the data source for the $/task column; license field reads NOASSERTION, so read the LICENSE file before copying.

name: BerriAI/litellm
why: Proxy that tracks spend per key; F15 names it as a documented way to attribute Claude Code spend. Borrow: a per-run key as the unit for cost attribution (check whether it can also cap spend); F7 lists LiteLLM's hardcoded reasoning-effort regex and non-comparable effort settings among its harness problems. License field reads NOASSERTION, so check the LICENSE file before copying.

name: frankbria/ralph-claude-code
why: Autonomous loop around Claude Code with a dual-condition exit gate (completion indicators AND an explicit EXIT_SIGNAL), a circuit breaker for stuck loops, hourly call limits, session expiry and git backup branches. Lessons from its changelog: a timeout (exit 124) was once misread as the 5-hour API limit (#183), and .ralphrc was changed from sourced to parsed-as-data for security (#346). Borrow: the exit-gate and circuit-breaker design for unattended runs; its 784 tests are self-reported.

name: snarktank/ralph
why: The plain Ralph pattern: each iteration is a fresh instance with clean context, and memory lives only in git history, progress.txt and prd.json until every PRD item passes. Borrow: fresh-context-per-iteration plus file state as the answer to context rot (F3 self-conditioning, F4 forgetting); the README gives no success or cost numbers, so test it on our benchmark.

name: ulab-uiuc/AgentDebug
why: Taxonomy (17 error types in 5 modules), 200 annotated failure trajectories and the AgentDebug pipeline from F5. Borrow: the taxonomy as the label set when the auditor classifies the kit's own failed runs, and the earliest-critical-error idea for retros; the dataset is on Google Drive, so check its terms.

name: chroma-core/context-rot
why: Scripts to replicate Chroma's context-rot report: needle-in-haystack variants, LongMemEval and repeated-words tasks at growing input length. Borrow: a cheap probe to measure how our agents degrade as context fills before choosing compaction thresholds; it tests plain chat prompts, not agent loops, and the last push is Sept 2025.

name: YangzeLiu/eval-instrument-disclosure
why: Reproduction scripts and maintainer reports behind F12, with dated correction notes after HAL's maintainers replied (a September per-model reordering claim was withdrawn on 2026-11-01). Process lesson to borrow: publish evaluator-audit checks (fraction of episodes graded, cost from root spans, evaluator version pinned) and date every correction; no license, so read only.

name: METR/vivaria
why: METR's former evaluation and elicitation platform (task standard, web UI, CLI); archived, and its README says METR is moving its internal tooling to Inspect. Lesson: even the group behind F1 retired its own harness, so build the kit's benchmark on a maintained runner (claude plugin eval, Inspect) rather than a custom platform.

name: microsoft/lost_in_conversation
why: Simulation code and data for F16 (sharded underspecified multi-turn tasks, 200,000+ simulated conversations). Borrow: the sharding idea for testing how a builder copes with a spec that arrives in pieces, and the aptitude vs unreliability split for reporting.

name: facebookresearch/meta-agents-research-environments
why: Meta's ARE platform and Gaia2 benchmark (F26): environments with verifiers, asynchronous events and time limits, budget-scaling curves. Borrow: per-scenario cost caps and a cost-vs-success curve in the kit's scorecard; the time-limit split shows slow models failing for latency.

name: earino/identical-runs-different-results
why: Data, code and delivered programs for F24 (584 runs, 52 repeats per pairing). Borrow: the repeat-until-resolved design and the compliance check beside the quality score; a data and analysis archive, not a framework.

name: headroomlabs-ai/headroom
why: Context-compression layer for tool outputs and logs (library, proxy, MCP server), named in F23 as a similar approach to its harness-side cost cuts. Borrow: the idea of trimming stale tool output before it reaches the model; its savings claims are its own, untested here.

name: microsoft/AgentRx
why: Code for AgentRx (F39): constraint checks over failed trajectories to localise the first unrecoverable step; a candidate post-run diagnosis tool for the kit's failure logs. Repo has no description; not read

name: METR/RE-Bench
why: METR's RE-Bench tasks (named in V37 as a source of the MALT transcripts); the repo is archived and has no description, so check its README and licence before relying on it. Not read
